utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Mr. Aleksic, you want to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Bearing in mind yesterday's ruling of the Trial Chamber, we are hereby withdrawing our yesterday's motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's the motion for an extension of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... withdraw it. Thank you. Mr. Ivetic, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Our next witness is Mr. Milivoje Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mihajlovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. You will now be examined by Mr. Ivetic on behalf of Mr. Lukic. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Mihajlovic. For the record, could you first introduce yourself to the members of the Trial Chamber, giving your name in full.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Milivoje Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And during the preparations for your testimony here, did you have occasion to meet with the Sreten Lukic Defence team to prepare a written statement?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance, I would like to have a hard copy of 6D1530 handed to the witness for efficiency of proceeding through this part of the examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I could ask you first to take a look at this document and see if, indeed, you recognise this as being the written statement which you prepared with the members of the Sreten Lukic Defence team for use in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have occasion to review the statement to ensure its contents accurately and correctly reflected your words and knowledge on the topics reflected therein before signing the same?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, today you're under oath. If I were to ask you today about these same topics and questions, would you still give the same answers and information as reflected herein in this written statement?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would move for Exhibit 6D1530 to be admitted into evidence. I don't believe there's any exhibits that are referenced therein, so it's just a free-standing statement at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mihajlovic, I would like to ask you some additional short and concrete questions in addition to your statement. First of all, what can you tell us about whether there existed in 1998 and 1999 radio or TV stations in Pristina broadcasting programmes in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: There was Radio Pristina and TV Pristina, and they all belonged to the Pristina TV media outlet and they had broadcasts in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. I was waiting for the transcript. And who sponsored or financed these stations that comprised Radio TV Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Radio TV Pristina was financed by the state of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how many hours a day did these stations transmit programmes in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Radio Pristina had 16 and a half hours of Albanian broadcasts a day, and as for TV Pristina they had three and a half hours of Albanian broadcasts a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you briefly or generally describe for us what time of programming comprised the -- both the TV and the radio broadcast schedules of these two stations.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Both TV and radio had information programmes, that is to say news; then they had entertainment, cultural programmes on television; they also had films; and on radio they had drama.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in your written statement at paragraph 7, that's page 3 of the Serbian, 3 and 4 of the English translation, you state that there were around 25 different magazines and newspapers in the Albanian language that were -- that were officially known of. Were these available in 1998 and 1999; and if so, where could they be obtained or purchased at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were sold on all newsstands in the province and one could buy them in every town in the province.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were any of these 25 that you have identified magazines and newspapers that were owned or financed by the Serbian or Yugoslav officials or authorities?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Except for a journal called Buj ku which was published for farmers initially and later on it had serious political articles which was financed privately until 1998; all other publications were state financed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you state that some of these were even KLA mouthpieces. What sorts of things did these Albanian-language newspapers or magazines have to say that led you to believe that they ought to perhaps have been banned even though they were not?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: There were two papers with information content which suited the KLA purposes, one was a weekly called Kombi, which means nation in translation, and there was a biweekly publication called Gazeta shqiptare. These publications mostly brought announcements of the KLA, they also published interviews of KLA commanders from the vicinity of Kosovska Mitrovica and throughout the province. These texts were such that they inspired ethnic hatred and it was strange for me that authorities did nothing to ban them. One could buy these magazines on all newsstands throughout the province in addition to magazines and publications in Serbia and in addition to all other available media.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One correction for the record, Your Honour, at page 4, lines 20 through 23, I believe that the witness testified that Bujku was published for farmers initially and later on it had serious political articles privately financed probably until 1998 although the publications were privately financed as I believe is what the translation came through. We can ask the witness to verify. All others were privately financed or we can have the witness clarify. I wasn't listening to the English translation, so I don't know if that's what actually came through on the text or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you tell us how the original or the journal you referred to as Bujku was published?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Initially it was financed by the state. Later on when they started having serious political content they became private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what did you say was the source of funding for all other publications?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could move to a related theme or topic at paragraph 36 of your statement, which I believe is the 12th and 13th page of the English and I believe the tenth of the Serbian or thereabouts. You talk of programmes of the Albanian TV Sele [phoen] programme telling people to leave Kosovo. First of all, who operated this TV broadcast?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That was the state television of Albania, TV Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you could tell us as based upon your observations in 1998 and 1999 how prevalent were the satellite receiver antennas in Pristina necessary for one to follow or watch this satellite TV programme of the Republic of Albania?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Almost every household, every apartment, in Pristina had a satellite aerial in order to be able to follow the programme of TV Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you have knowledge of -- you have -- you've identified the subject matter of the calls that were put forward on this TV broadcast. Do you have knowledge of why that TV broadcast explained or told people to leave Kosovo-Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: TV programme constantly informed about the crisis in Kosovo and Metohija, and at the very outset of the bombing and before the bombing started in their media there was information to the effect that there soon would be a war between NATO and Yugoslavia, based upon which they concluded that they needed to leave Kosovo as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In addition to the programmes that we have been talking about thus far, do you also have any knowledge of any illegal radio stations that transmitted or operated within the territory of the province -- the Serbian province of Kosovo and Metohija during 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: In mid-1998 and in 1999 there were also illegal radio stations. One was called Slobodno Kosovo or free Kosovo, which broadcast in news in Albanian and music, and that station constantly guided the sentiments of the Albanian population in the province. They aired interviews of local KLA commanders, and in some critical moment they called upon the people to leave their villages and to go someplace else. They were known as a mouthpiece of the KLA literally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you say they aired the interviews of local KLA commanders. Do you know the area where this free Kosovo or Slobodno Kosovo radio station operated or transmitted?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't know from which place that programme was broadcast, but one could listen to it on radios in the greater part of Kosovo, in Drenica, in Metohija, in the area of Kosovska Mitrovica, one could follow the signal of that radio station, of those radio stations, very well. I guess that there were a number of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment. Is it -- in its name it used Serb language, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, they used Albanian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's appearing in our transcript as called Slobodno Kosovo. Is that not Albanian -- Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In translation in Serbian it's called Slobodno Kosovo. In Albanian it was known as Kosova Elire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mihajlovic, you said at lines 22 and 23 of page 7 you guess there are a number of them. Do you have any actual personal knowledge of any other names of any such private or illegal radio stations transmitting in various regions as mouthpieces for the Kosovo Liberation Army or any other armed Albanian separatist faction?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That radio was known as Slobodno Kosovo and every broadcast began with the following words: You are following radio Slobodno Kosovo or you are listening to radio Slobodno Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm finding this difficult in the interpretation that we're constantly in English getting the name Slobodna Kosovo. Can the interpreter help us and explain why that is the translation into English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, sometimes it's a custom to keep the names in the original. The literal translation into English would be: Free Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Please continue, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mihajlovic, if we could turn to your media centre in Pristina itself. Could you please tell us how and by whom it was decided to form this media centre.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: The media centre was established by an association of journalists in Serbia which was the only association of journalists in the republic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were you a part of this association that decided to form this media centre or I should say are you one of the driving forces of the efforts to have the media centre established?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was one of those who gave the initiative to establish the media centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were there Albanian journalists who were members of the association?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the association of journalists of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were Albanian journalists, not many but there were some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I guess -- I believe it's in his statement, but just if you could clarify the media centre in Pristina that you ran included Albanian staff in addition to Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the Pristina media centre about 20 people were employed, the majority of them were Serbs but there was several Albanians and there was even a woman from Syria.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how were the directors and other officers of the media centre selected?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: The Association of Journalists of Serbia established a programme board of the media centre that elected director and editor-in-chief and we selected other employees of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How was media centre financed? How did you obtain funding for the same?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: The media centre organized press conferences, and those who held press conferences had to pay and that was the main source of funding for the media centre. And the journalists who were employed in the media centres also worked occasionally as stringers or freelancers, and they would earn thereby money, 15 per cent of which was due to the media centre and that was sufficient to fund the work of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you also have to seek out any donations from private firms?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have to look for donations, but about ten private companies gave donations to the media centres in the following form. We received a Xerox machine, we received curtains and some other equipment and the premises remained there in the media centre, original premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mihajlovic, you say that those who held press conferences had to pay. What do you mean by those who held the press conferences? Can you give us examples so that we can see the relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Conferences were held by leaders of oppositional and other parties in Serbia, all of them had to pay 500 marks for each press conference at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were there also foreign entities that would also rent the press centre facilities for use for press conferences?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There were foreign organizations that rented out the premises, they were mostly NGOs who wanted some publicity because at the media centre at any time there were at least 100 to 150 journalists present.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe in your statement you describe the accommodations with the Hotel Grand for the use of the media centre at -- I think that's at paragraph 10 at page 4 of the English. Now, did you -- how did you obtain the necessary equipment, gear, and other technical details for the media centre, apart from the premises, since you've already had that detailed?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have already said that we received a printer as a donation from a company in Valjevo. We received several TV sets as a donation from some private companies, either in Serbia or in Kosovo. We bought our own telephones. We did not have much in terms of equipment. We only had three computers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now all inclusive including all the salaries and expenses for the various personnel there, what was the monthly cost of operations for the media centre?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Salaries amounted to about $1.000 a month for all employees. As for retirement contributions and other costs, that did not go over $2.000 a month. So the entire operation cost about $3.000 a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever send any reports relating to the work of the media centre to anyone; and if so, who?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every month we would send reports on the work of the media centre to the Association of Journalists of Serbia who was our founder, and then we also sent to them an annual report at the end of each year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, did you have contacts with the OSCE-KVM and what kind of cooperation did you provide to them?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: We had good cooperation with the OSCE and with the KVM because they spent quite a lot of time in the Grand Hotel and they communicated both with us and with the journalists who were staying or who were in that hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 28 of your statement, that's in the Serbian page 9, in the English I'm showing, page 4 -- that can't possibly be right. I believe in the English it should be approximately page 10 if I'm not mistaken, you mentioned that you had dinners with the America KDOM chief Shaun Byrnes. With respect to those dinner meetings did Mr. Byrnes at any time ever voice to you any concerns about the level of cooperation from the Serbian MUP and particularly from Sreten Lukic of the MUP staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, he did not complain about the cooperation with the Serbian police. Most often we talked about the two journalists from Radio Pristina who had been kidnapped, Perenic and Slavuj. Mr. Byrnes insisted on meeting their families. These journalists have not been traced to this day, but Mr. Byrnes never said about having bad cooperation with the police. To the contrary, I think that he mentioned that he had good cooperation on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just one last question with respect to Mr. Byrnes. During these same dinner meetings did he ever voice complaints to you that the Serbian police were committing widespread violence and/or crimes against the Albanian citizens of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention that. It was my impression, at least that's what he used to say, that his job was to place local KLA commanders under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move on now. Who was your main contact person within the Serbian Ministry of the Interior and from what organized unit or structure of the Serbian MUP did that person hail?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: My main contact was the spokesperson of MUP, Bozidar Filic, who worked in the Pristina SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were there any incidents when you took either domestic or international reporters out into the field when you were attacked by the KLA or other armed Albanian separatists or criminal movements?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was an incident in late July, that's the one I remember, in late July of 1998. As we were returning from Orahovac there was a column of some 40 vehicles comprising mostly representatives of the foreign media outlets. We were on our way back from Orahovac and we came under attack. Part of the column was severed and they turned back, whereas two vehicles in one of which I was continued to Pristina. The third vehicle was a jeep with BBC personnel was hit by a round. In addition to that I told you that KLA members kidnapped journalists of TV Pristina, Slavuj and Perenic. These two people have not been found to this day, and also a journalist from Tanjug, Nebojsa Radosevic and his cameraman who were released after 25 days in captivity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to spend time in or reside in Kosovo Polje; and if so, for how long and when?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I lived in Kosovo Polje from the age of 5 and then all the way up to the end of June 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us in terms of its geographic size or layout how large a town Kosovo Polje is?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Kosovo Polje is a municipality that had a population of 12.000. It has one main street that goes towards Pristina from that neighbourhood and a few smaller streets. The railway station of Kosovo Polje is the main building there -- rather, it is the railway hub of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, we've had some witnesses here, specifically Generals Vasiljevic and Gajic, who have claimed that the paramilitary groups, first the Wolves of the Drina and then also Arkan's Tigers, were based in Kosovo Polje. First, as someone who hails from the region and lived there during the relevant time-period and as someone who professionally was a news journalist covering events in the region, could you comment on your opinion of the feasibility of these assertions?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I think that that is not realistic. Kosovo Polje is only 6 kilometres away from Pristina. In Pristina there were 2.000 foreign journalists in that period, 1998/1999. That could not have been concealed. I never heard of such information and I lived in Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 15 of your statement, that's page 5 of the English, you describe terrorist attacks that were carried out "according to the same model." How often or frequent were these types of attacks that you said were carried out according to a particular model?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, these attacks usually took place in mid-1998 and in the second half of 1998 practically every day between Djakovica and Pec, Pec and Klina, Pec and Prizren and Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just to clarify one matter, you mentioned at page 14, lines 12 through 16, that the municipality of Kosovo Polje had a population of 12.000. Would I be correct that the actual town itself has a much smaller population?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, the town itself had a population of 12.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you have any -- strike that. We've had some evidence here about the death -- or actually the murder of an individual by the name of Kelmendi, Bajram Kelmendi, a noted attorney from Kosovo and Metohija. Do you have any personal knowledge or information into this incident; and if so, from whom and what is that information?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I knew Bajram Kelmendi. I know that he was killed in Pristina in his very own apartment. We carried that piece of news at the media centre. Later on we heard in town that Bajram Kelmendi had been killed by criminals, a mixed Serbian and Albanian gang. I have no proof, but that is what people were saying in town and also a lot of money was taken from his safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to speak with any members of his family regarding this?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I talked to his wife after his death; she was terribly shaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was she able to confirm any of the details that you have just mentioned about what was being heard in the town relating to this individual's death?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this was right after his murder. He was murdered and his son was murdered in the same house. She was terribly shaken. We just exchanged a few sentences about that. She had heard these stories that went around town, but we didn't have any proof.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mihajlovic, for coming to give testimony. I think I told you in proofing we put a lot of your stuff into the written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, that's all I have for direct examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mihajlovic, was it only one son that was killed along with Kelmendi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, if I remember correctly it was one son only. I'm not sure, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Any Defence counsel have questions? No. You'll now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in addition to Serbian, what other languages to you speak and understand?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Albanian and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In your statement, Exhibit 6D1530, there are a number of things I wanted to ask you about. In paragraph 3 you mentioned that "the KLA appeared in the media with a statement in 1997 in which it accepted responsibility for a terrorist act." And then you say: "The political leaders of the Kosovo Albanians, above all Ibrahim Rugova, the," here it's translated as DSK leader ignored the appearance of the KLA for a long time, claiming that it did not exist and that it was the product of the Serbian secret services." In your statement there where you say "the political leaders," how many people are you talking about and who exactly are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Primarily Ibrahim Rugova, then the vice chairman of his party Fehmi Agani; then Adem Demaqi, who was a very influential Albanian politician, then a few politicians who were not as influential as Ibrahim Rugova, that was Ljuljeta Pulja Beciri, Kaqusha Jashari, and Jusuf Buxhovi, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you're saying each and every one of those claimed that the KLA did not exist; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: In 1997, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And then in 1998 did they start to come around and say that the KLA did exist?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 Adem Demaqi became the spokesperson for the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, didn't the Serbian authorities for just as long a time, if not longer, deny the existence of the KLA; as a matter of fact, for years they used the term "so-called KLA," right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll object to the form of the question. This is a peculiarly I think that the Trial Chamber's raised in certain languages -- and I think it's improper to imply that "so-called" has the same meaning in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you see, that's a matter the witness can handle, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A matter of assessment, opinion, judgement, it's not a black-and-white situation where you can say that the question is improper. So, Mr. Hannis, if you consider there's any value left in your question, please proceed with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 6 you mention that the press in Albanian which came out in Kosovo supported the KLA. And you say the dailies Bujku and Koha Ditore did not condemn the attacks in the province. Is it your evidence that neither one of those papers ever condemned the attacks carried out by KLA, they never condemned the violence; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: In the period from 1997 through 1999 not a single newspaper in Albanian condemned a single terrorist attack that had been committed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you saying that Koha Ditore never took Mr. Rugova to task for not taking a stronger position against the violence committed by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's not to say that they condemned violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. According to paragraph 7 you say there were 25 newspapers and magazines in Albanian being published in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mention Kombi and Gazeta shqiptare as being literally the mouthpieces of the KLA. So I take it that Bujku and Koha Ditore were not mouthpieces for the KLA, were they?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No. Bujku and Koha Ditore transmitted KLA statements or press releases, but they did not carry interviews with the leaders and commanders of the KLA and they did not disseminate hatred.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 you say: "It's interesting that in these magazines," and I think you're referring to Kombi and the Gazeta, "they only used the derogatory term to refer to the Serbs." I can't pronounce that word, but I would like to ask you in your reporting, what term did you use to refer to the Kosovar Albanians and the KLA, did you use the word "Albanac" or "Siptar"?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Albanac only.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And is that because you used -- you viewed the use of the word "Siptar" as derogatory?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No. The term Siptar is not derogatory. When the Albanians say it themselves that they are Albanian, they say: I'm an Albanian --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness spoke in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- this is not a derogatory term, but in the Constitution of Serbia, the Albanians were called Albanians, Albanci. I know there were some Albanians who were upset when they were called Siptars, so that's why I called them Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You, in referring to some of these publications in paragraph 7 you say: "It was obvious that these newspapers were not able to sustain themselves on the number of copies printed and sold but received assistance from the outside." How was it obvious? Did you take account or do an accounting of those newspapers?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: It was obvious because there were ads in these newspapers, ads that were under the slogan: The homeland is calling.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness again spoke in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this was in support of the Albanian cause in Kosovo as they put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Didn't your media centre receive assistance from the outside as well?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean assistance from the outside?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you talked about donations and equipment received from private companies; wasn't that from the outside?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, well, that is from the outside in the form of three TV sets and three computers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's the total -- that's the sum total of what you received from private companies?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's all we received from private companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You didn't receive any financial donations?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no need for financial donations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say in that paragraph 7 that: "It was assumed that some of them," these Albanian publications, "like Koha Ditore were funded by international organizations." Assumed by whom, by you?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Assumed by all, Albanian journalists, Serb journalists. There were even texts in the press that was published in the Albanian language in Pristina stating that the Koha Ditore paper was financed from abroad. Zeri i Rinise in particular said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you do anything independently to check that out for yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't try and I really had no way of checking either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 10 you explained how on 16 April 1998 you launched the media centre in Pristina. How did you come to do that at that time? Why?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: At that time the number of foreign journalists coming to Pristina was on the rise. Every day there were more and more of them. These people had no place where they could send their reports from and they didn't have a particular centre where they could receive assistance for what they needed. I thought that chaos and misinformation should be prevented and I thought that the opening of this kind of a centre would be justified from a professional point of view, professionally justified.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was that solely your idea?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was my idea and it was a few years old, but before that I did not stand a chance of doing that because I had a lot of work for different media. So in my view that was the last moment when the media centre could have been set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was there no discussion about doing this with the Ministry of Information, either at the republic level or in the province if there was one at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no discussion. The then-minister of information never visited the media centre in Pristina. In the provincial government there was a secretariat for information, but they either did not have the capacity to do that or the wish to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what individual or individuals are you talking about in the secretariat of information? Can you give us their names?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Bosko Drobnjak, secretary for information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you mean, Mr. Mihajlovic, by the provincial government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The authorities in the province, the Executive Council of Kosovo that existed at that time, in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who in April 1998 was head of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In April Veljko Odalovic was head of the district, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In that paragraph 10 you mention: "We had the tacit agreement of people from the government." What do you mean by "tacit agreement"?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That they wouldn't create any problems for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And who exactly were the people in the government you're referring to there, is that the same Bosko Drobnjak or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, regardless of whether it's the secretariat for information or someone from the party that was in power, they could have created problems for us if they wanted to. If they wanted to, they could have told the manager of the hotel not to give us premises for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who in the party are you referring to then, can you give us some names?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the party at the provincial level or the local Pristina level. It depends who'd be bothered by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you said you had the tacit agreement of people from the government. Who in the party are you referring to by name?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Vojislav Zivkovic, president of the SPS of Kosovo and Metohija primarily, he was a journalist beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did he facilitate the arrangements for you in the media centre to have offices at the Grand Hotel?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You said: "We were allotted offices." What exactly allotted those offices to you?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: The manager of the Grand Hotel, his last name was Djorovic, I can't remember his first name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you have to pay for those rooms?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No. He knew that once the media centre was opened all the journalists would be guests of his hotel, and quite literally once the media centre was opened there was not a single free room at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And business at the bar probably improved greatly, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You say in paragraph 9 -- I'm sorry, at paragraph 10: "My goal was to try to help so that as little blood as possible would be spilled in Kosovo, knowing that the media could calm the situation." In what way did you see the media calming the situation?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I thought, and I still think, that in calming the situation the most important thing is for the media to tell the truth, not to make comments and not to add oil to the fire in critical times and at flash-points of crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you almost took the words out of my mouth. I was going to ask you if in your experience as a professional journalist, wouldn't you agree that often the media calms the situation the way gasoline calms a fire?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 11 that: "All operations by the police against terror by Albanian separatists were condemned by the international community." I agree with you that the international community, for example, in the form of United Nations resolutions, two of them in 1998, did condemn police actions. But was it your experience that the entire international community condemned all operations by the police?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: These resolutions obviously show that they pertained to all police actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, in the terms of those resolutions themselves, weren't they limited to what they described as disproportionate use of force against civilians, not all force but disproportionate force against civilians, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 17 you talked about an event in the village of Opterusa and you mention a German reporter Renata Flotau talking to the victim of that crime. Do you know, did she write a report on that?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if she wrote a report on that. I just know that she found the victim and talked to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In connection with her, in paragraph 26 you talk about foreign journalists behaving in different ways, "there were those who came to Kosovo with a set task, constantly searching for stories on how Serbian police were killing Albanian children and true professionals who wanted arguments and proof for everything." How would you classify Renata Flotau, was she a true professional or was she one of those others that you describe?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what I managed to read in terms of what Renata Flotau wrote, I think that she was a rather objective journalist. I say rather objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you find her rather reliable in terms of what she wrote?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already said that there was 2.000 or 2.500 journalists there during that one year, and I did not really have much time to check each and every one's reliability.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see the story she wrote in Der Spiegel in April 1999 about what she described as Mr. Rugova's house arrest?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think I did see that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you do anything to try and check out whether that story was accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Ibrahim Rugova's house. I took a group of several foreign journalists there when the Russian ambassador went to see Rugova, I think his last name was Kotov and I think his first name was Yuri, he was the Russian ambassador to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if you recall the story that Renata Flotau wrote about that, that was the very occasion when she managed to escape from the house during that occasion when journalists were brought with the Russian ambassador, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No. I found her in Ibrahim Rugova's house, and we exchanged a few words while the journalists were filming Ibrahim Rugova and the Russian ambassador. She wanted to know whether her car was still parked in front of the Grand Hotel. I don't think she felt the need to escape with the journalists because a day or two previously another group of journalists had visited the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You weren't aware that she had been in the house with Mr. Rugova for several days before that occasion? You didn't know that, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You in paragraph 18 say: "The conduct of the media in Albanian at this time was strange." I have a little trouble with the English in that sentence. It's not clear to me, do you mean the conduct of the media in the Albanian language; is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I was referring to. I thought and I still think that it's very strange when the media failed to condemn violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you say: "There was no condemnation of crimes and only crimes against Albanians were constantly emphasised," right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So they are condemning crimes but only the ones in which they say Albanians were victims, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And wouldn't you agree with me at this time that couldn't some Kosovo Albanian journalists say a similar thing about the Serbian media, that is, that they were reporting only crimes by Albanians against Serbians?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, there were Serbian media who condemned only crimes against Serbs, but there were other media which also condemned crimes against Albanians, very seriously, very sharply.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And which Serb media were those?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Vreme, Nin, Danas, Blic and probably some others in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in Kosovo were there any Serbian media that was condemning crimes allegedly committed by Serbs against Albanians?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Radio Pristina condemned crimes against both Albanians and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You say in paragraph 20 that: "While the media centre was in operation from 18 April 1998 to 28 June 1999, all the news was written solely by me."

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So how many people worked at the media centre? I think you said before something like 20 people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you were the only one that was writing any reports that went out from the media centre?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How many articles or reports did you issue from 18 April 1998 to 28 June 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know precisely, but on the average five to eight news items per day on events in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this is on top of all the travelling you told us about, how you were out in the field often, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I have a question. You say to 28 June 1999. You stayed another ten days or so after the Serbian forces left?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say: "No one ever issued a denial for a single news item." What do you mean exactly, that no one ever --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No individual ever complained about a story you wrote?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't write stories. We only did news items, and no one ever denied or challenged any single fact from those news items, either in the domestic or the foreign media. And when I refer to domestic media I'm referring to media both in the Albanian and the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I just have a question here. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: What were your sources for all this news that you got because you were all the time in the Grand Hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't in the Grand Hotel all the time. I was also on the field and my sources were my colleagues, journalists, all over Kosovo, also the directors of clinics and hospitals in the region, the chiefs of the districts, the heads of districts, the presidents of local communes or municipalities, my colleagues, Albanians from the area. When I got information from one source, I had to check it with another source, verify it, and that's how I obtained my information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that between sometime in March 1999 until June 1999 there wasn't really any Albanian media up and working in Kosovo, right? All those publications had been shut down and most of those reporters and writers had left or were in hiding, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: There were no other media apart from the radio stations, the radio Free Kosovo. Other media were not published because there was no freedom of movement in the province due to the NATO air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And Free Kosovo radio never disputed any of the news items you wrote during that time?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have time always to listen to their news, but I didn't deal with that. They mostly issued KLA communiques.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us earlier when you were talking about the media that was available in Kosovo, you talked about TV Tirana constantly broadcasting a message for the Albanians to leave before the war. How often, how frequently, were you listening to TV Tirana during that time-period?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't do that very often, maybe once or twice a week; however, the broadcasts of TV Tirana were spread around very quickly so that all my colleagues, both Serbs and Albanians, would tell me what Tirana had said on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Regarding your sources in addition to the answer you gave Judge Chowhan a little while ago, did you not have sources in the MUP that sometimes provided you information?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And those sources in the MUP included some sources from the DB, the state security, side of the Ministry of Interior, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, my source was Bozidar Filic, and he confirmed information or denied information I had received from the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, my question was in the plural, sources. So are you saying your only source from the Ministry of the Interior was Bozidar Filic and no one else?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when it came to Pristina and large-scale clashes, there was also a certain Colonel Sipka from Prizren who gave me information as to what happened in Orahovac when there were big clashes in Orahovac; or also people from the municipal police units on the ground when we were there with our journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about from the VJ, did you have any sources in the VJ in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 in the VJ communication with the media was dealt with by a man whose last name was Zirojevic, I don't know what his first name was, but from time to time he communicated with journalists, he did so very infrequently though.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you had no other source of information from the VJ other than him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I think that's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 21 you talked about doctors from the hospitals in Kosovo being a reliable source.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe the most reliable source.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But you would agree their information is limited due to the fact that they would only know about the people they actually saw and treated, correct? They couldn't tell you about wounded or killed who were not in their hospitals, not in their offices, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And would you agree in 1998 and 1999 that there were a number of Kosovo Albanians who might be reluctant to turn themselves in to the hospital for fear of being suspected, maybe correctly or incorrectly, as terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I think your statement is only partly true. The wounded had to go to a hospital, otherwise they would die afterwards. There were no illegal or local hospitals in that area that we knew about. Most of the wounded were in the regular hospitals where they could get the best medical assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from all your sources including the MUP and the VJ you never heard anything about field hospitals or independent doctors who were treating terrorists and Kosovo Albanian civilians outside of the normal hospitals?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I did hear there were such hospitals, but they treated mainly KLA members. I don't think they treated civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what's your basis for saying that, that they didn't treat civilians? Who's your source?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: My sources about this are my Albanian colleagues, journalists, and also foreign journalists who had frequent contacts with KLA members and commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, is this the time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, you have another 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I can't keep track of our schedules when we move around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned in that paragraph that you had requests from the police not to publish names about killed or wounded until they had a chance to inform the families. That makes sense. You say they also requested that you delay publication so the families could be officially notified. Did you report the names of Kosovo Albanians killed during these anti-terrorist operations?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever I was able to obtain the names I published them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you an exhibit now, it's Exhibit P3121. Well, I'm sorry, let me withdraw that and move on to something else. I need to come to that later. You say in paragraph 22 that: "Generally everyone gave positive assessments of the centre's work." I assume from that that not everyone did. Who didn't give positive assessments?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: It was only the information centre of Ibrahim Rugova who didn't and on only one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You mention a particular German reporter named Erich Rathfelder?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Rathfelder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I think this your statement it's spelled Ratfelder, R-a-t-f-e-l-d-e-r, but from news stories on the internet it appears his name may be spelled R-a-t-h-f-e-l-d-e-r. And you talk about him in connection with a story about Orahovac. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is it true that you personally spoke to him after that story came out by him and told him that it might be better if he left because his safety couldn't be guaranteed?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from whom was he endangered?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: At that point I thought the greatest threat to him was the fact that he had published false information which had no basis in fact and that this information had in a way been ordered. And I felt that the greatest threat to that journalist came from the people who had convinced him to write that text in the way he did. I thought it had been commissioned from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this in the statement, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes -- well, Your Honour, I think I'm looking now at paragraph 22, but I think the first reference to this is in paragraph 18. The witness says: "I remember an example when journalist Erich Rathfelder who reported for several German papers wrote an article on the alleged existence of a mass grave in Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that after the war in I think July 1999 there was a German forensic team who went out to interview an individual who had reported that information to Mr. Rathfelder?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And to actually do some digging in the area of Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware of a story that Mr. Rathfelder wrote after he left Serbia shortly after this incident in July or August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So you didn't tell him that he might be in danger from angry Serbs because of the story he had written about Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't tell him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 27 that: "Members of international organizations, the OSCE, KVM, and others, bombarded the public with news of the abuse of Albanians. It was as if Serbian civilians did not exist." In addition to the OSCE and the KVM, what other international organizations are you talking about there? Do you include the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the ICRC was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you include Human Rights Watch?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you follow the Kosovo portion of the trial of Mr. Milosevic's case?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about this trial, have you followed this trial at all on TV or in the media?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You are not familiar with the testimony of a Human Rights Watch employee named Fred Abrahams?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you weren't aware of a report he wrote about Serb victims in Kosovo in 1998/1999?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that report, I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So you have not reviewed all the KVM reports or all the reports of those international organizations, have you?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I haven't reviewed them. It was my job to take the journalists where they said there was a mass grave for them to see whether there was or wasn't a mass grave there. I myself did not know whether there was or was not a mass grave at that particular place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me stop you. I'm not talking about Orahovac right now. I'm talking about your statement in paragraph 27 when you say: "It was as if Serbian civilians did not exist" and how members of all these international organizations bombarded the public with news of abuse of Albanians. And I'm just trying to get at the basis of your opinion for stating that. The fact is you have not reviewed all those materials because if you had, you would have seen that some of those organizations were writing about Serb civilians as victims.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see anywhere the information that about a dozen villages in Metohija had been emptied of Serbs, that there were no longer any Serbs in those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 36 you talk about when the NATO bombing started and that there was fear of the bombs, fear of the KLA, among the Albanians there was fear of the police and the army fighting against the KLA. That was a problem for many of the Albanian civilians, wasn't it, the fighting between the army, the police against the KLA because civilians sometimes got caught in the middle, got injured or killed, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could never distinguish on the ground civilians from the KLA to a large extent. There were people who wore civilian clothes but carried weapons. You could see that from the cars even when we were driving along the roads towards the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 37 you mention that you published news on BBC that the police arrested over 700 people who had committed crimes. When did you publish that report approximately if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact date, but I think it was in May 1999. I received this information from the chief of the Kosovo district, and this information was heard at the session of the interim Executive Council which was held on that day or the day before and this was a rather reliable source of information regardless of the chaos prevailing in Pristina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So from the chief of the Kosovo district, would that be Mr. Odalovic or are you talking about Mr. Andjelkovic? I'm not clear on the --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Odalovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And did that information have a breakdown of the types of crimes for which those 700 people were arrested?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So you don't know if any of those 700 crimes were war crimes against civilians, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I think they were different kinds of crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know that -- whether the majority of them were for theft and property-related crimes?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 38 that on the day that the Kumanovo Agreement was signed, the streets of Pristina were suddenly full of Albanians, which convinced me that only a small number had left Pristina." Were you not in Pristina every day basically in March and April of 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Not all day, but mostly in the evening I would be in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in your travels from the field and from home to and from the media centre during that time-period, you didn't notice hundreds or thousands of civilians being directed toward the train station?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't observe them being directed. I did, however, see groups of people going in the direction of the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Huge groups of people, right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's say dozens of people in a group, just as I saw groups of people moving towards the railway station in Kosovo Polje and towards the bus station in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did Mr. Filic share information with you from the MUP about the number of Siptars or Albanian -- Kosovar Albanian civilians who had left the country in the first four or five weeks of the war?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he did. We received information of that type from the foreign media, who reported larger and larger numbers every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you accept their reports as credible?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I had no possibility of transmitting those -- that information. I could only see that CNN and other stations were broadcasting this information, but I did not have any opportunity to go and see for myself in Macedonia those camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you didn't make any inquiry of your sources from the VJ or the MUP about the number of civilians that had left or were leaving?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't have many contacts with Mr. Filic at the time. I saw him very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we take the break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In a moment, yes, Mr. Hannis. Was there no reporting from the border or the area near the border by Serb media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I can explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, I'd be interested to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbian media from Pristina found it very difficult to move to the borders with Albania and Macedonia because parts of the road were cut off and they couldn't move. There were check-points held by the police in some places, by the KLA in others, so you couldn't pass through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We need a break at this stage, Mr. Mihajlovic, so while we have that could you please leave the courtroom with the usher and we shall see you in 20 minutes. We shall resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mihajlovic, would it surprise you to learn that in a MUP report of the 1st of May, 1999, it was being reported by the MUP staff in Pristina to the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade that approximately 715.000 Siptars had left the country by April 30th of 1999? You were aware that those kind of numbers of people were leaving, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that a number of people were leaving the province, but that figure would surprise me because at that point I thought the number was just too high.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But you have no reason based on your personal experience to disagree with what's in the MUP reports, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: If that is an accurate information, then I have no reason to disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you an exhibit, it's P3111, this is a photograph, and I want to ask you if you can identify any of the people in this particular photo.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise the guy who I guess is sitting in blue T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Second from the left on the front row?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who is he, what's his name?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I think this is the cameraman of Associated Press. I think his name is Srdjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know his last name?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's Nedeljkovic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the Associated Press from where? Do you know what office he was from?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's Associated Press from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you not recognise any of the other people in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you about where your offices were in the Grand Hotel, what floor were you on?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: My offices were on the first floor of the Grand Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from April 1998 until June 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware of in the summer of 1998 a number of politicians coming down from Belgrade, specifically Mr. Minic, Mr. Andjelkovic, Mr. Matkovic, and Mr. Sainovic? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it wasn't only them. Numerous ministers from the Government of Serbia used to come as well as vice-deputy prime minister Vuk Draskovic, all of them would come occasionally to Pristina and I would normally see them either at the Grand Hotel or at some public functions that they attended. Naturally Milutinovic, president of Serbia, came to have talks with Albanians a bit prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware of a creation of a body known as the temporary or provisional Executive Council for Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who was a member of that as far as you knew or who was the head of that?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran Andjelkovic headed the provisional Executive Council, and as for members there was Bosko Drobnjak for information. For information of minorities the name of the member -- he was a journalist from the Roma desk of Radio Pristina. I can't -- I will remember his name a bit later, it will come to me. And I think that they were split up in various fields, agriculture, economics. I remember the name of the person for agriculture and then there were various other fields that people were in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware or did you ever hear of a body called the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija? Have you ever heard that term?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and in 1999 I never heard of that term and I didn't know that there existed some sort of a Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question is: Did you ever hear of the term before today?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I think that I read in some Belgrade papers recently, in recent months, about that term; prior to that, I didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you -- how often did you see Mr. Minic, Mr. Andjelkovic, and Mr. Matkovic, and Mr. Sainovic in Kosovo in 1998, let's say between July 20th and the end of October 1998, just during that time-period, how often would you see them?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps five or six times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have nothing against these questions, but if somebody poses a question relating to a group: How many times did you see four people, then that insinuates something because previously the witness spoke about there being more politicians. Well, why doesn't he ask about five persons rather than four. Did you understand what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Hannis, that this has to be put in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. I was trying to save time, but I think I lost it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How often during that time-period did you see Mr. Sainovic between mid-July 1998 and the end of October 1998 in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps three or four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And during that time were you in Pristina every day?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Almost every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think you told us before, especially in the evenings, right, because you might be out in the field during the day?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you about an incident that occurred in the area of Donje and Gornje Obrinje at the end of September 1998. Do you know what I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which one you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You're not aware of an event in which it was alleged that a number of civilians had been massacred by Serbian forces in the area of those villages around the 26th of September, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Could you help me with this, how was this done?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, there was a lot of international press about this event. You don't recall it?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me how that event came about and then it will come to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it's alleged that several members of a family called Delilaj, D-e-l-i-l-a-j I think is one of the spellings, including a few small children under the age of 10 were killed during the anti-terrorist actions in that area. And you don't know about that?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: If this involves a group of people who were killed on a trailer -- on a tractor-trailer, then yes, I remember that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, it's not on a tractor-trailer, it's in their homes and in the forest where they were running and hiding around their home. That still doesn't ring a bell for you?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me show you Exhibit P2827, if I could. This is a memo to President Milutinovic from the deputy minister of information. That's the cover sheet, and if we could go to the next page in both English and B/C/S. You see this is dated I think the 1st of October, 1998, and the deputy minister is advising President Milutinovic that: "Reports in the western media and in the Albanian press about an alleged massacre of Albanian civilians by Serbian police in Gornje Obrinje village in Kosovo has assumed the proportions of a campaign in the international media." And the second paragraph says: "It's obvious that the publicity about the alleged massacre is media manipulation." And near the third paragraph starts: "Officials of the Ministry of the Interior deny that its members conducted operations against civilians, adding that an investigation would be launched." If we could go to the third page of the English. "An investigation would be launched into the alleged crime which they learned about from the Western media." So the MUP knew about it, the deputy minister of information knew about it and was reporting it to President Milutinovic. You didn't know about it?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. Most likely I had a news report on this, but I don't remember this particular event. There were quite a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Quite a lot of them that reached the level of the president of the republic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, I think that may be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, sir, I will advise you that this matter was also discussed in a meeting of the Supreme Defence Council on the 4th of October, 1998, with Mr. Milosevic, but I guess --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
