utterances.text: Underneath the heading of this document. Underneath the heading there is DJ/AK. I can explain why it was written that way, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Those are your initials, AK?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: So I was present when the interview took place, I was present throughout, but I was not present when the record was written. The record was compiled by Dragan Jenic, my colleague, and that is why my name is not on the record because I was away on official business at the moment when the record was being typed out, but my initials are there as proof of the fact that I attended and that I conducted the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, wasn't the interview conducted by the deputy war crimes prosecutor, Stankovic; is that I think what you said earlier in chief?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: Dragoljub Stankovic was present, he worked together with us, that is to say that this interview was conducted by Dragan Jenic, myself, and Dragoljub Stankovic, the three of us that is to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. And if we could move on to P2824 -- well, we don't really need to see that or to get into that exhibit. May I just ask you this: Were you involved in the case charging certain police officers or former members of the MUP for participation in concealing bodies in Petrovo Selo? This case I think was heard in 2007.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: What case are you referring to specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We have a record, and that is the one in front of you, which is a transcript of the testimony of Bozidar Protic before the war crimes chamber of the Belgrade district court, and this is in respect to the case relating to bodies found at Petrovo Selo. Were you a party to that particular investigation or that case?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: I was a party in two cases concerning Petrovo Selo, the mass grave in Petrovo Selo, and the murder of the Bytyqi brothers. These are two cases linked to Petrovo Selo and this is why I asked you which case you were referring to specifically, whether the Bytyqi brothers or the mass grave in Petrovo Selo case. The two cases are linked, but I can't see from this which of the two this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not the Bytyqi brothers, the mass grave. Can you look at the reference number and not know if you were involved in that case, it's the top left hand of the document.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: That's the number of the district court, it doesn't mean anything to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: So I can't identify the case by that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know that Protic testified in the Belgrade district court in respect to Petrovo Selo in 2007?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: That's the -- for the investigating judge, he's competent to do that. He -- I assumed he testified, but now we're talking about proceedings before an investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: May I clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not Protic testified? Do you know that he testified?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: Protic told me when I talked to him that he had testified more than once before investigating judge Milan Dilparic, so I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is it the Belgrade district court?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: Yes. He is the investigating judge of the court for war crimes in Belgrade, and you can see that in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is the war crimes chamber of the Belgrade district court the same as office of the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: The war crimes chamber is part of the Belgrade district court, it has trial chambers or trial judges and investigating judges. In the chamber there are two investigating judges and several trial judges, the war crimes chamber, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this the only page we have?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. It's probably -- could we move on to page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: See if there's a reference there to the status of the judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you tell us from that record whether or not this transcript relates to a trial or the proceedings of an investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: This is a transcript before the investigating judge -- in fact, I think so because I haven't seen the judge who signed this. No, excuse me, it says "presiding judge," then it must be the trial. I do apologise, it must be the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It also says it's a trial.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it's probably the Bytyqi brothers trial because the mass graves case is still in the investigation stage, whereas the Bytyqi brothers case is in trial now. That's why I asked you what case this was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you spoken to Protic since the 8th of February, 2007?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I spoke to Protic before he came to testify before the Hague Tribunal because the service for the detection of war crimes is authorised to act on requests coming from The Hague Tribunal and the investigating judge and he was to be a witness. My interviews with him in that period were about that because he refused to appear as a Prosecution witness, and I then tried to explain his role to him and to explain to him that he was duty-bound to respond to the summons from the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many drivers did you interview in respect to the allegations that bodies were transported from Kosovo to Serbia and concealed?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: I can't give you the precise number, but everyone who participated in it, less than ten who had direct or indirect knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Protic is one driver.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the others that you interviewed?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: I may have misspoken. Everyone who participated in the transport, not just the drivers but those who were providing security as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... drivers three times. I am asking you about drivers. No, I understand that you may have misspoken. Very well. Did you interview any other driver apart from Protic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: The drivers, no, but the security, yes, the people who sat with them in the vehicles. Somebody was driving the vehicle and he was the driver, if one might put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But Protic said as driver -- well, we won't go into that. I just wanted to know about the drivers. You spoke about two cases that your team investigated, one being the Suva Reka case. You handed over the file in 2002?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: In 2003, that's when we handed over the file to the prosecutor's office for war crimes, that's when that office was established. That's when we completed the police investigation and established precisely what had happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, the indictments, you know, were issued in that regard in 2005 -- sorry, on the 25th of April, 2006. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: Yes, when the prosecutor's office received that material they requested from the investigating judge an investigation, and then from 2003 to 2005 the investigating judge conducted an investigation based on the documentation submitted by the MUP. Based on that documentation, it was established that there were grounds to suspect that some people perpetrated a crime and these people were arrested, seven persons were arrested subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You mean you are saying that it took the prosecutor three years, approximately, between the time when you submitted your records to study them and then based upon those records indict, or is it that the prosecutor had to conduct his own investigation?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR KOSTIC
utterances.text: No. The prosecutor submitted a request to the investigating judge. It was the investigating judge who conducted an investigation, and it's true that it lasted for two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. I have nothing further for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kostic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Just one point that I perhaps should have picked up earlier. Were you personally involved in the investigation of the finding of bodies at Petrovo Selo or is your personal involvement confined to the Suva Reka case and the Bytyqi brothers case of the cases that you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I participated personally in all the cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to correct the transcript, on page 81, 4, 5, 6, it was said that the indictment in this case was issued in March 1999 and became public in March 1999, which is incorrect, it was May. 81, 4, 5, 6, my learned friend Mr. Stamp --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, Your Honour. We finished this witness right on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kostic, that does complete your evidence. Thank you for coming to assist us. You may leave the courtroom with the usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall resume here at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
